sections.heading: How to Play Augmentation
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Augmentation"][color=c13]Augmentation Evoker Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
At its most basic, the bread and butter of Augmentation gameplay is all about weaving together your key damaging abilities and group buffs in order to maximize the damage output of your group. Here are some of the big ideas to consider while playing Augmentation:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_sarkareth size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c13]Keep your buffs up:[/color][/b] Augmentation's rotation is centered around maximizing uptime of [spell=395152]. [spell=413525] allows us to extend the duration of Ebon Might through our damaging rotation: casting [spell=408092] and [spell=357208] at appropriate ranks on cooldown, spending resources on [spell=395160], and filling downtime with [spell=361469] (or [spell=362969]).
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_livingflame size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c13]Always be casting:[/color][/b] Keeping high uptime on your rotational spells is key to maintaining a solid resource economy in both raids and Mythic+. Use [spell=358267] effectively to cast spells on the move, and make sure to fill any "downtime" in your rotation with your filler spells, Living Flame and Azure Strike, in order to deal damage and generate [spell=359618].
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_essenceburst size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c13]Watch your Essence Burst:[/color][/b] Augmentation Evoker has a few different potential sources of [spell=359618], and the buff only stacks up to 2. Make sure to spend your Essence Burst when capped, ideally before casting [spell=359618] generators like [spell=409311] and Living Flame to avoid wasting resources.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_breathofeons size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c13]Mind your cooldowns:[/color][/b] It's often correct to send cooldowns as soon as they've come back up, but look for opportunities to align your major cooldowns like [spell=403631] with allies' cooldowns and big damage moments during an encounter.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority

[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=classicon_evoker_augmentation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon] Best Augmentation Evoker Rotation[/h2]
At its core, Augmentation Evoker follows a simple spell priority aimed at maximizing uptime of buffs on allies. Augmentation spends its resources while buffs are active to extend buff duration, and spends its downtime replenishing resources before starting the cycle over again.

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Augmentation Evoker: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
	Before any combat happens, it is important for Augmentation Evoker to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
	[center][wrapper width=800px][center][box]
	[ul]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Check Consumables -[/b] Any or all of food, flask, weapon oil, augment rune, as needed. [/li]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Cast your Raid Buff -[/b] Use [spell=364342] to buff you and your raid or party with cooldown reduction on major movement abilities. This buff lasts for an hour.[/li]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Apply Source of Magic -[/b] Cast [spell=369459] on your chosen healer. This buff lasts for an hour.[/li]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b](If talented) Apply Blistering Scales -[/b] Cast [spell=360827] on your chosen target; this will usually be the tank in group content, or yourself in solo play. This buff lasts for an hour, or until removed.[/li]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b](If talented) Draconic Attunements -[/b] Check to make sure you have your preferred [spell=403208] active. [spell=403264] is generally the default choice.[/li]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b](If talented) Apply Timelessness -[/b] Cast [spell=412710] on your chosen target; this will usually be a DPS player that generates high amounts of threat. This buff lasts for an hour.[/li]
	[li icon=exclamation-circle][b](If talented) Cast Bestow Weyrnstone -[/b] Cast [spell=408233] on your chosen target. This generates an item in both players' inventories which can be activated in combat.[/li]
	[/ul]
	[/box][/center][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_firebreath type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Empower Spells [/color][/h3]
The key to making the most of [spell=357208] and [spell=408092] as an Augmentation Evoker is ideally to ensure that you [b]only cast these abilities while [spell=395152] is up[/b] in order to extend the duration of [spell=395152], as well as direct [spell=413984] towards nearby buffed allies.

Casting [spell=357208] at higher Ranks increases its upfront damage while reducing the duration of its Damage over Time (DoT) effect. Additionally, the Evoker class talent [spell=369939] benefits from casting [spell=357208] at higher Ranks by increasing the number of [spell=361469] projectiles. Each projectile deals full damage and has an individual chance chance to generate [spell=359618]. Even in single-target, this can cleave onto injured allies and have additional chances to grant [spell=359618] assuming there was effective healing.

While this interaction is valuable, casting [spell=357208] at a higher Rank without [spell=370553] requires additional cast time, potentially delaying other spell casts like [spell=396286]. If upranking [spell=357208] would delay [spell=396286] or otherwise cause [spell=395152] or [spell=1259173] to expire early, it's best to simply cast [spell=357208] at Rank 1 and continue to spend resources as usual. As a general guideline, consider casting [spell=357208] at Rank 1 if [spell=396286] is off cooldown, or if there is less than 4-5 seconds of buff duration remaining on either [spell=395152] or [spell=1259173].

In summary, [b]consider casting [spell=357208] at Max Rank when suitable[/b], in order to maximize value from [spell=369939], otherwise simply cast at Rank 1.

Empowering [spell=396286] simply expands the radius of the spell's area of effect, so [b]in single-target situations Rank 1 [spell=396286] is entirely sufficient[/b]. In AoE situations, you will want to uprank [spell=396286] such that as many enemies as possible are within the area of effect.

[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Tip The Scales" icon=ability_evoker_tipthescales]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_tipthescales type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Tip The Scales [/color][/h3]

[b]You can choose to pair [spell=370553] with either of your Empower spells[/b]: [spell=357208] to deal damage more quickly and benefit from [spell=369939], or [spell=396286] if the additional radius is beneficial. Since casting [spell=357208] at Max Rank is always useful, this is generally the default pairing.

Remember that using [spell=370553] always saves a small amount of time over casting Empower spells normally, even at Rank 1. More importantly, it makes the Empower spell cast instantly, activating the spell sooner and allowing you to cast while moving.

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color] Tip The Scales[/minor-heading]
[pad]
When playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color], it is especially important to note that [spell=431695] activates when [spell=370553] is first pressed, but its cooldown does not begin until the buff from [spell=370553] is consumed.

Be sure to treat [spell=431695] from [spell=370553] as a major DPS cooldown and cast it alongside your [spell=403631] and other major cooldowns when they naturally align. Otherwise, essentially aim to cast [spell=370553] on cooldown.  With [spell=404977] talented, every other cast of [spell=370553] can be immediately followed by [spell=404977] to benefit from stacking cooldown reduction. More on this in the Advanced Tips section below.

[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Ebon Might" icon=spell_sarkareth]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_sarkareth type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Ebon Might[/color][/h3]

[spell=395152] is Augmentation's main group buff on a baseline 30-second cooldown, which encourages you to [b]cast this ability as often as possible while aligning with the DPS cooldowns of other players[/b]. When [spell=395152] is down, it is generally best to take the time to build resources and hold onto abilities which extend [spell=395152] until your next [spell=395152] window is active.

[spell=395152] is beholden to the "pandemic" mechanic of duration extension, meaning that you can cast [spell=395152] while it's active and add the remaining duration onto the new spell cast, provided that this is less than 30% of the base duration of the buff. [b]It is ideal to re-cast [spell=395152] with no more than 3-4 seconds remaining[/b] in order to minimize wasted uptime. 

The amount of main stat granted by [spell=395152] currently updates dynamically to reflect changes in the caster's Intellect stat, but does not currently update to reflect player deaths or removed buffs.

[minor-heading type=bar toc=false][symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color] Ebon Might[/minor-heading]
[pad]
When playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color], it is important to note that it can be correct to re-cast [spell=395152] early in order to try to proc a [spell=431874] Critical Strike. This most commonly occurs immediately after channeling [spell=404977], in which case you should immediately cast [spell=395152] again despite having a full duration on the buff. In this situation, you are sitting on a full set of resources and are not risking any [spell=395152] uptime by "casting too early", meaning this a strict benefit.

[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Breath of Eons" icon=ability_evoker_breathofeons]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_breathofeons type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Breath of Eons[/color][/h3]

The ideal usage for any individual cast of [spell=403631] involves aligning the 10-second Temporal Wounds window with the highest-burst windows of your buffed allies' DPS rotations. However, practically speaking, it is more likely that you will[b] aim to cast [spell=403631] roughly on cooldown[/b] to maximize uses, assuming some non-zero amount of damage contribution from your buffed allies.

While raiding, make sure to be flexible with the exact timing of [spell=403631]. Mythic raid encounters, for example, often have very specific timings where players choose to use their DPS cooldowns, including damage amplifications, shield phases, add phases, and other mechanics. Being aware of these key timings can help maximize your buff output with [spell=403631].

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Time Skip" icon=ability_evoker_timeskip]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_timeskip type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Time Skip[/color][/h3]

While [spell=412713] can be used in all PvE content, it comes at the cost of a capstone talent point. This means that Augmentation Evokers will occasionally find additional value taking other capstone talents and instead playing [spell=404977].

[spell=404977] naturally encourages you to set up windows where multiple strong abilities are all on cooldown, at which point channeling [spell=404977] results in tremendous value returned over a number of different spells. 

It is currently recommended that you first use [spell=404977] [b]during your opener and following your first set of Empower spells [spell=357208] and [spell=408092].[/b] This timing maximizes your cooldown reduction, applies [spell=413984] to two additional targets, and provides additional burst damage through your damaging spells. This timing also maximizes cooldown reduction value from [spell=404977] during your [spell=431695] window when playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color].

After your first cast, consider using [spell=404977] essentially on cooldown, aligning with [spell=431695] whenever possible (as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color]), and ideally when channeling [spell=404977] will reduce the cooldowns of [spell=357208], [spell=408092], [spell=409311], and [spell=403631] by the full duration.

[pad]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c13][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon] Augmentation Evoker Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[pad]
[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Buff Targeting" icon=Ability_evoker_prescience]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Prescience[/color][/h3]

	In Midnight Season 2, Augmentation Evoker is returning to a buff-focused playstyle where a larger portion of the spec's damage specifically comes from buffs on allies. [spell=409311] in particular will play a bigger role in Augmentation's damage profile in Season 2 due to a mix of stat priority, talent choices, and the new tier set effect which buffs [spell=412774].

	While [spell=409311] will prefer to automatically target nearby players with cooldowns active, there are a number of reasons why two players in cooldowns might see a substantial difference in buffed damage. Things like player skill, target counts, damage profiles, even how their specs scale with Critical Strike can affect how much value is obtained through buffing one player over another with [spell=409311]. Ultimately making the most of [spell=409311] will require some degree of preparation using tools like WarcraftLogs in order to identify which players are dealing the most damage throughout a given fight.

	When you're ready to advance from exclusively auto-targeting [spell=409311], consider starting by choosing 2-3 of your strongest dps players to buff consistently throughout the fight. Once you're comfortable manually targeting[spell=409311], you might consider targeting specific players on pull or during key burst windows, while buffing other players with more flat or consistent damage profiles outside of cooldowns.

	Tracking [spell=409311] in combat can be a challenge, and it is highly encouraged for you to set up your UI in whatever way works best for you. The spell [spell=361021] can be toggled on and tracked to help indicate when players are currently in their major cooldown. Additionally, certain addons allow for the creation of "spotlight frames", which are essentially a separate smaller group of unit frames that can be managed separately from your main raid frames; this can be especially helpful to help you focus on buffing specific players.
	[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Positioning for Buffs" icon=ability_evoker_masterytimewalker]

	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Shifting Sands[/color][/h3]

	Another consequence of stacking Mastery in Season 2 is the renewed importance of [spell=413984]. When casting an Empower spell, [spell=413984] applies to the nearest ally without [spell=413984] already active, preferring DPS players. This means that [b]your positioning matters[/b] and as a rule of thumb you should aim to stand as close as possible to the players dealing the most damage whenever possible.

	When playing with 2 or more Augmentation Evokers in the same raid, it is especially important to ensure that you stand as far apart from each other as possible so as to avoid buffing each other with [spell=413984], as this would generally result in a substantial damage loss.

	Positioning for [spell=413984] is not always entirely practical, but is extremely important to understand, as it can be very rewarding under the right circumstances.

	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Motes of Possibility[/color][/h3]

	There are some considerations to make when playing with [spell=409267]. Firstly, the actual motes themselves prefer to spawn in a rather large cone in front of where the player character is facing. This means that standing in a specific location and facing a specific direction can influence roughly where the motes will spawn and the path they will take as they slowly move towards you. 

	While this is likely to be even less practical to play around perfectly in practice, understanding the behaviour of [spell=409267] is rather important. With [spell=1250914] talented, [spell=409267] have a 50% chance to grant either [spell=409311] or [spell=413984], which are both substantial damage buffs in Season 2. [spell=409267] does not have any smart targeting; this means whoever picks up the mote gets the buff, including tanks, healers, yourself, or other Augmentation Evokers.

	In raid, you will want to encourage your other dps players to pick up these motes whenever practical, and for non-dps players to avoid them. As with [spell=413984], if you are playing with 2 or more Augmentation Evokers, you will also have to contend with motes spawned by other Evokers, and will want to avoid those motes as well as your own.

	In Mythic+, generally your two allied dps will have solid uptime on both [spell=409311] and [spell=413984] through your base rotation, and as such it's generally sensible for your tank to pick up any motes that travel through melee and are convenient to grab. Otherwise, as long as your healer generally tries to avoid picking up any motes, there's not too much else you can do to optimize here.
	[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Tip the Scales" icon=ability_evoker_tipthescales]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Cancelaura Macros[/color][/h3]
	When playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color] with [spell=404977] talented, ensuring that the cooldowns of [spell=370553] and [spell=404977] remain in sync is particularly important, as the two spells need to be used together in order to benefit from stacking cooldown reduction when casting [spell=404977] with [spell=431695] active. Since the cooldown of [spell=370553] does not begin until its buff is consumed, you may run into issues whenever an Empower spell is not immediately available to cast. The easiest way to play around this is to set up a macro to immediately cancel the buff from [spell=370553]. This does not affect [spell=431695] in any way, and allows [spell=370553] to immediately start its cooldown without delaying any important casts.

	Here is an example of what such a macro might look like:
	[code]#showtooltip
/cast Tip the Scales
/cancelaura [known:Temporal Burst] Tip the Scales[/code]

	Simply press the macro once to activate [spell=370553] and then immediately a second time to cancel the buff.

	Note that this only results in a significant damage gain when playing the [spell=404977] variant of [symbol=wow-hero-talent-chronowarden] [color=#ddad44]Chronowarden[/color] talents. This is less required when playing with [spell=412713] talented, in which case [spell=370553] can generally be used on cooldown without needing to cancel the buff.
	[pad]
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]
[pad]

Our Augmentation Evoker guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Augmentation Evoker guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].

[tooltip name=prescience][color=q]Prescience and Ebon Might are removed upon pulling a Raid boss or starting a Mythic+ keystone. Do not ever cast these abilities pre-pull.

Prescience can be cast while targeting specific players, but will otherwise choose a target automatically if the player is targeting an enemy, preferring DPS players with active cooldowns. In Season 2, manually targeting Prescience is more valuable than in Season 1, so consider targeting strong players whenever possible, especially during key moments such as on pull or during important burst phases. Avoid capping Prescience charges, and feel free to use Prescience outside of Ebon Might to generate resources, as Prescience itself does not extend Ebon Might.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=blistering][color=q]From a damage standpoint, Blistering Scales is generally not worth casting in place of damaging spells during combat. Unless your tank is in immediate danger from melee swings or similar effects, try to cast this spell before the start of a pull, between packs in dungeons, or otherwise during downtime. Recasting this spell is not needed if the Regenerative Chitin talent is selected.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=firebreath][color=q]Cast Fire Breath at Max Rank to benefit from Leaping Flames granting additional chance to activate Essence Burst. Avoid upranking Fire Breath if doing so will delay Upheaval or cause Ebon Might or Duplicate to expire early. You should generally avoid casting Fire Breath if Ebon Might is not active.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=upheaval][color=q]You should generally avoid casting Upheaval if Ebon Might is not active.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=eruption][color=q]You should generally avoid casting Eruption if Ebon Might is not active. That said, if Essence Burst is about to expire, it can still be worthwhile to cast an Eruption in place of a filler spell to benefit from effects like Ignition Rush and Momentum Shift.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=prepull][color=q]Prescience and Ebon Might are removed upon pulling a Raid boss or starting a Mythic+ keystone. Do not ever cast these abilities pre-pull.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=eons-cw][color=q]As Chronowarden, cast Breath of Eons before Ebon Might in the Opener for an extra chance to activate Double-time.

Always have a plan for casting Breath of Eons. You typically want to choose the shortest path possible that avoids dangerous mechanics, as well as choose an end location that positions you near ideal buff targets and sets you up for upcoming mechanics. Keep in mind that your flight only needs to make contact with the enemy hitbox; you don't always have to fly directly through the center of the target in order to hit, especially when it comes to large bosses![/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=eons-sc][color=q]As Scalecommander, remember to push Breath of Eons a second time\u2014or use a cancelaura macro\u2014to stop flying once you've hit your targets.

Always have a plan for casting Breath of Eons. You typically want to choose the shortest path possible that avoids dangerous mechanics, as well as choose an end location that positions you near ideal buff targets and sets you up for upcoming mechanics. Keep in mind that your flight only needs to make contact with the enemy hitbox; you don't always have to fly directly through the center of the target in order to hit, especially when it comes to large bosses![/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=trinkets][color=q]The best time to use your active trinket depends on the type of trinket you're using. Trinkets that provide on-use Critical Strike should generally be cast before Ebon Might for Double-time value. Other on-use stats including Mastery are generally best used as soon as you land from Breath of Eons. Trinkets with a substantial cast time or mini-game can depend but are often used before casting Breath of Eons in order to maximize damage output during the damage amplification window.[/color][/tooltip]
